I recorded the successful seven-minute Android playback test in the [media proof](/Users/pkerschbaum/.codex/worktrees/3529/cup/.scratch/social-signup/issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md) and updated the [draft specification](/Users/pkerschbaum/.codex/worktrees/3529/cup/.scratch/social-signup/spec.md) to retain the HTML player. I also corrected the spec to reflect that the **web PKCE prototype passed**. Markdown validation passes.

The remaining auth proofs are local OSS Supabase setup and Google disconnect behavior. The next product decision is how the open trial result moves to its account copy.

❓ **Q1 — When the copy becomes ready:** Should the app keep playing the original and offer **“Open your private copy”**, switching only when tapped? I recommend that, with playback resuming at the same position. If copying fails, the original stays available and the page offers **“Retry copy.”**
Q1: I would say if the user had a trial conversion and does the sign up, we just stop the playback. Not best UX, but the convert-from-trial-to-real-user case is anyways a rare case, an exception!

That makes the transition simpler. I’ll record signup as an explicit playback stop, while keeping the trial result accessible during the copy. The remaining choice is what the page shows while copying and when the private copy becomes ready.
